quarterly_data.quarter: Yamaha Motor results briefing Q&A: First Half FY2026 Briefing and Q&A Minutes (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A, CEO Motofumi Shitara and Executive Officer Mitsuru Hashimoto presenting): the full-year forecast projects a record-setting JPY 260 billion operating profit; the OLV (Outdoor Land Vehicle) business is expected to post a JPY 40 billion loss this year including JPY 12 billion of one-time structural-reform costs (some incurred in H1, the majority expected in H2), and the company aims to make up significant ground next fiscal year and return OLV to profitability by 2028. The main H2 risk factors assumed are rising raw material costs linked to the Middle East situation and changes to U.S. tariff policies, with results possibly coming in below or above projections; the Medium-Term Management Plan is proceeding smoothly and the company aims to meet or exceed its targets.
quarterly_data.figure: full-year operating profit forecast JPY 260 billion; OLV loss JPY 40 billion incl. JPY 12 billion one-time costs

quarterly_data.quarter: Yamaha Motor results briefing Q&A: First Half FY2026 Briefing and Q&A Minutes (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): Robotics performance is strong on higher demand mainly around semiconductor back-end processing equipment, and demand for surface mounters is also up in China. However, companies in the industry face memory supply challenges and risk shortages of certain components, so the key is how much of this demand the company can capture; demand and the market environment remain bullish and capturing it is a big opportunity.

quarterly_data.quarter: Yamaha Motor results briefing Q&A: First Half FY2026 Briefing and Q&A Minutes (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): Q2 operating profit was driven by very strong motorcycle sales, mainly in India and ASEAN (firm demand in Indonesia, India and Vietnam), with the shift to premium-priced models raising the average price per unit and profit ratio; raw material costs are rising, and the weak yen and tariff situation worked in the company's favor versus the original forecast. New motorcycle launches are planned notably for India, Vietnam and Indonesia, and higher unit sales are expected in H2; management expects continued growth in the premium segment. Part of R&D spending has been postponed into H2 while investment criteria are reviewed, with resources focused on high-return areas rather than across-the-board cuts.

quarterly_data.quarter: Yamaha Motor results briefing Q&A: First Half FY2026 Briefing and Q&A Minutes (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): OLV structural-reform costs cover promotions to clear inventory after the discontinuation of in-house ROV production, compensation to suppliers for changed development plans and ceased production, and workforce optimization; the company will concentrate on ATVs and golf cars, cut fixed costs, and address the remaining JPY 28 billion deficit through cost cuts and golf car product competitiveness to return to profitability in 2028.

quarterly_data.quarter: Yamaha Motor results briefing Q&A: First Half FY2026 Briefing and Q&A Minutes (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): Marine Products profit rose on price increases, with large H1 contributions from Asia and Latin America, where the company has a high market share; the U.S. and Europe remain major profit sources, and the business is being restructured to secure profit even with flat developed-market sales. Marine demand is stable and an upward jump is expected from economic stimulus such as interest rate cuts. As large-horsepower interest has expanded from the 400 hp class to models exceeding 600 hp, the company is strengthening its lineup and preparing to launch new large outboard models in the upcoming season, which it expects to recover market share and improve the model mix from next fiscal year.
